summary: M0 model-only verdict: ESCALATE @ 0.75. Case ho-08 for g.sen@aegean.edu shows a phishing email (edevlet-burs-basvuru.com, subject "KYK burs ödemeniz beklemede") delivered at 13:02:44 on 2026-10-15 followed by a user click at 13:10:09. This represents a potential credential exposure. However, the subsequent sign-in activity shows no signs of account takeover: all logins originate from the same device (dev-gs-phone), same city (Manisa, TR), and only two expected networks (AS34984 Superonline off-campus with MFA, AS-AEGEAN-EDU on-campus without MFA). No new devices, impossible travel, MFA fatigue, or anomalous access patterns are observed. The phishing click is a concrete exposure event rather than a weak signal, but there is insufficient evidence to confirm compromise or to fully exonerate the account. A human reviewer should determine whether to force a password reset, inspect mail rules/forwarding, and assess whether credentials were harvested on the phishing site.
limitations: M0 ablation: Nemotron alone, no tools, no Critic, no Risk Gate, no DQ. Not a product configuration.
